decision_flags.title: Resection recommended before PET-CT result?
decision_flags.concern: The clinician proposed VATS resection while the PET-CT is only being scheduled, and a tissue diagnosis, pretest malignancy risk estimate, and PFT results were not available. Methotrexate use and RA could also complicate the picture, since they raise infection and inflammatory nodule possibilities.
decision_flags.consider: Consider deciding on resection after the PET-CT and PFTs, with a formal malignancy risk estimate, and discuss options such as biopsy or surveillance and a multidisciplinary review.

evidence.quote: i'm going to go ahead and suggest that we do remove this
i'm also going to schedule a pet ct

decision_flags.title: Is the stated smoking rationale adequate?
decision_flags.concern: The decision to operate was based on the smoking history, but pack-years were never quantified and he quit seven years ago. The nodule is smooth with no emphysema, which is somewhat reassuring.
decision_flags.consider: Consider quantifying pack-years and risk-stratifying (size, location, margins, age) before attributing the surgical recommendation to smoking history.

decision_flags.title: Perioperative methotrexate plan not addressed
decision_flags.concern: The clinician simply said to continue the RA therapy, with no plan for perioperative methotrexate management, wound healing or infection risk, or coordination with the rheumatologist ahead of surgery.
decision_flags.consider: Consider discussing perioperative methotrexate handling with the rheumatologist and anesthesia if surgery proceeds.

decision_flags.title: Informed consent and patient's fear

decision_flags.consider: Consider reviewing risks, alternatives, and next steps in more depth and allowing time before consent.
